instrument: Augmented ALTAI coding codebook (19 original ALTAI sub-principles + 8 inductively derived CDA/nested sub-principles)
source: Sub-principle definitions 1-19 adapted from the HLEG (2020) Assessment List for Trustworthy AI. Definitions 20-27 reproduced from the manuscript's own Tables 3 and 4 (construct boundaries and illustrative audit evidence).
unit_of_analysis: A component is an atomic prescriptive step, requirement, control, test, checklist question, or outcome criterion extracted from a single framework document.
decision_rule: Assign zero or one code per component. If a component maps to more than one sub-principle, assign the single best-fitting code based on its primary/dominant requirement. If a component does not fit any of the 27 sub-principles below, assign code 0 (UNMAPPED). Do not code purely illustrative or descriptive statements that contain no prescriptive requirement, evidence expectation, or decision criterion.

sub_principles.name: Human Agency and Autonomy
sub_principles.definition: Addresses how the AI system affects human behaviour, decision-making, and perception. Covers whether the system creates confusion about algorithmic involvement, generates over-reliance/automation bias, or risks manipulating users through simulated social interaction.

sub_principles.name: Human Oversight
sub_principles.definition: Examines governance mechanisms enabling human intervention in AI operations: human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, or human-in-command approaches, including operator training, detection mechanisms for erroneous outputs, and override/stop capability.

sub_principles.name: Resilience to Attack and Security
sub_principles.definition: Assesses vulnerability to adversarial attacks, cyber threats, and malicious use, and evaluates protective measures against data poisoning, model evasion, and model inversion attacks across the system lifecycle.

sub_principles.name: General Safety
sub_principles.definition: Covers risk identification, measurement, and mitigation across use cases: threat/hazard assessment, safety criticality levels, fault-tolerance planning, and criteria for when the system requires re-evaluation.

sub_principles.name: Accuracy
sub_principles.definition: Focuses on ensuring the system's predictions/outputs maintain appropriate precision for their use case: data-quality requirements, ongoing accuracy monitoring, and communicating performance/error expectations to users.

sub_principles.name: Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility
sub_principles.definition: Evaluates consistent performance across contexts and conditions: verification/validation methods, fail-safe/fall-back procedures, handling of low-confidence outputs, and management of risk from continual learning or model drift.

sub_principles.name: System Design and Development
sub_principles.definition: Structured engineering practices that reduce defect/unsafe behaviour before deployment (e.g., hazard analysis, safety cases, secure-by-design). Boundary: not the same as Reliability/Accuracy (outcome metrics) nor Traceability (documentation); focuses on process controls and design artefacts. Evidence: design controls (e.g., STPA/FMEA records, model/spec reviews), signed safety case or assurance argument, change control and design history file, secure checkpoints for ML.

sub_principles.name: Performance and Monitoring
sub_principles.definition: Ongoing, post-deployment surveillance of model/process performance in live context. Boundary: distinct from Reliability/Fallback (capability) by requiring operational thresholds and intervention playbooks. Evidence: defined KPIs/guardrails with thresholds, drift/decay monitors, incident runbooks, rollback procedures tested in production-like environments.

sub_principles.name: Privacy
sub_principles.definition: Assesses the AI system's impact on the right to privacy and to physical, mental and/or moral integrity, and includes mechanisms for flagging privacy-related issues arising from the system.

sub_principles.name: Data Governance
sub_principles.definition: Examines data protection compliance and management practice: Data Protection Impact Assessments, privacy-by-design measures, data minimisation, implementation of data-subject rights, and alignment with data management standards.

sub_principles.name: Traceability
sub_principles.definition: Documents the development process to enable tracking of data, models, and decisions: ability to identify which training data, model version, and rules produced a given output, via continuous quality assessment and logging.

sub_principles.name: Explainability
sub_principles.definition: Enables understanding of how the AI system reaches its conclusions: technical process explanation and reasoning transparency, with particular attention to opaque ('black-box') systems requiring alternative accountability measures.

sub_principles.name: Communication
sub_principles.definition: Conveys system capabilities, limitations, and accuracy to users: disclosing AI involvement in interactions, explaining decision criteria, communicating risks, and providing user-facing training/explanatory materials.

sub_principles.name: Avoidance of Unfair Bias
sub_principles.definition: Prevents systematic errors that discriminate against specific groups: bias detection and mitigation across data collection and algorithm design, plus reporting mechanisms for identified bias.

sub_principles.name: Accessibility and Unfair Design
sub_principles.definition: Ensures the system serves diverse users regardless of age, ability, or other characteristics: universal-design principles and accessibility standards, particularly for people with disabilities and assistive-technology users.

sub_principles.name: Stakeholder Participation
sub_principles.definition: Incorporates affected parties into design and development: seeking regular feedback from those directly or indirectly impacted (including workers and community representatives) across the system lifecycle.

sub_principles.name: Environmental Well-being
sub_principles.definition: Evaluates ecological impact across development and deployment: energy consumption and carbon-emissions measurement, and reduction measures across the system's lifecycle.

sub_principles.name: Impact on Work and Skills
sub_principles.definition: Assesses effects on employment and worker capability: worker consultation, understanding of how the system changes work, de-skilling risk, and retraining/upskilling provision for affected staff.

sub_principles.name: Impact on Society at Large or Democracy
sub_principles.definition: Examines broader societal and democratic effects beyond direct users: potential harms to institutional integrity, electoral processes, or pluralistic values in society.

sub_principles.name: Auditability
sub_principles.definition: Enables independent evaluation of the AI system and its governing processes: traceability mechanisms, documentation practices, and third-party audit capability, without necessarily disclosing proprietary information.

sub_principles.name: Risk Management
sub_principles.definition: Establishes processes for identifying, documenting, and minimising adverse impacts: external oversight, ethics review, vulnerability-reporting mechanisms, whistleblower protection, and redress procedures for affected individuals.

sub_principles.name: Auditing Context
sub_principles.definition: Scoping and governance of the audit itself: system boundary, object of audit, assurance level, materiality, evidence strategy, and independence. Boundary: not Auditability (system's capability to be audited) nor Risk Management (control cycle); focuses on audit-specific scoping questions such as what is being audited. Evidence: approved audit plan (scope, materiality, criteria), evidence map (artefacts, sources, samples), independence statement, stakeholder access protocols, traceable linkage from findings to corrective actions.

principles.key_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)

sub_principles.name: Organisational Context and Strategy
sub_principles.definition: Links the AI system to business purpose, criticality, accountable owner, and success criteria. Boundary: not generic Risk Management; requires purpose, control and KPI alignment for this specific system. Evidence: system dossier stating purpose, need for AI, owner, criticality tier; control objectives; governance forum minutes showing alignment decisions.

sub_principles.name: Compliance and Legal
sub_principles.definition: Mapping of applicable obligations beyond data protection (sectoral, product safety, equal opportunity, financial conduct, medical device, etc.) with accountable owners. Boundary: distinct from Privacy/Data Governance; extends to non-data legal regimes. Evidence: compliance requirements with citations; legal applicability analysis; notified legal team of relevant adaptations or changes to the AI system.

sub_principles.name: Training and Awareness
sub_principles.definition: Role-specific capability to operate, monitor, and intervene in the specific AI system. Boundary: not generic ethics training; distinct from Auditability (system docs) by focusing on human readiness. Evidence: roles with learning outcomes tied to system risks; completion/assessment of training records; evidence of training updates after model changes.

sub_principles.name: Operational Context and Risks
sub_principles.definition: Environment/interaction constraints of deployment (workflows, interfaces, human factors, edge cases) and preparedness for disruption. Boundary: not solely Technical Robustness; emphasises socio-technical fit and operational hazards. Evidence: context-of-use analysis; HRA/usability evidence; failure mode libraries; scenario tests on real workflows; business continuity and incident playbooks referencing AI behaviours.

sub_principles.name: Third-party Risks
sub_principles.definition: Dependence on external models, data, vendors, or cloud services, including assurance inheritance and residual risk. Boundary: complements Risk Management by focusing specifically on supply-chain attestations. Evidence: supplier assurance pack (e.g., SOC/ISO mappings), model card/data sheet from vendors, contract clauses for updates/incidents/audit rights, results of third-party impact tests.

unmapped.name: UNMAPPED
unmapped.definition: Use when a component does not correspond to any of the 27 sub-principles above and is not merely illustrative/descriptive text.
